bull_bear.body:
- Repeat-order orientation built on service quality and a stated service guarantee, per the MD&A Outlook
- Asset-light service model with no manufacturing activity, so conservation-of-energy and technology-absorption disclosures are not applicable
- Breadth of advisory offerings spanning strategy, project, financial, AI/technology and transaction (M&A, syndication) work under one roof
- No borrowings from banks or financial institutions for any purpose, and no charge registered with the ROC (Schedule III additional regulatory information)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Talent attrition and wage inflation — MD&A: firms face ongoing talent attrition as mid-career professionals leave for equity incentives in venture capital or product management roles; demand for practitioners versed in AI governance, advanced analytics and ESG outstrips supply, inflating compensation and compressing project margins. For an asset-light advisory firm whose only productive asset is its consultants, this is the core structural risk.
- Bundling by large IT delivery players — MD&A: massive IT delivery players such as TCS and Infosys frequently package strategy with implementation, undercutting pure-play advisory firms by up to 30%, directly pressuring the pricing of a small pure-play consultancy.
- Clients building in-house strategy and transformation teams — MD&A: corporate clients are rapidly expanding their own internal strategy and transformation departments, and internal centres of excellence absorb routine advisory functions, directly reducing reliance on external agencies.
- Freelance and platform disintermediation — MD&A: independent contractors and freelance platforms offer highly specialised, on-demand expertise at a fraction of the cost, challenging legacy consulting models and forcing a rethink of pricing strategies.
- Shift to outcome-based pricing and the burden of proving ROI — MD&A: clients are moving away from hourly billing toward gain-share and outcome-based fee structures tied to measurable metrics, and are strictly results-oriented; justifying premium fees without demonstrable metrics or milestone-based contracts is increasingly difficult, which transfers delivery risk onto the consultant.
- Industry skill gap and pace of technology change, particularly around AI — MD&A: a significant skill gap exists in the industry which could lead to a loss of revenue, since service quality depends entirely on the expertise and knowledge base of the people employed; capabilities are simultaneously transitioning toward deep tech integration, requiring continuous upskilling of the legacy workforce.
- Geographic and single-market concentration in India — The Company operates mainly in the Indian market and the Directors' Report states it neither earned nor used any foreign exchange during the period under review, so results are undiversified against a downturn in domestic consulting demand. Recorded as a structural concentration risk although the report does not label it as a risk.
- Tax and regulatory compliance exposure — The Directors' Report discloses a GST Show Cause Notice (No. 04/CGST/R-V/RBD/2025-26) received from the Kolkata South CGST & CX Commissionerate in respect of the Company's GSTIN, to which the Company submitted a reply; regulatory change is separately named in the MD&A as an external risk category.

outlook.body:

- Partner with other firms through joint ventures, alliances or strategic partnerships to share resources and expertise as the Indian consulting industry becomes more collaborative
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no capacity addition, project, site or expansion programme for the Company. The Directors' Report states the Company is not engaged in manufacturing activity, so conservation-of-energy and technology-absorption particulars are not applicable, and refers only to 'editing facilities, offices etc.' where energy-conservation measures are taken. Schedule III additional regulatory information records that the Company has not borrowed any funds from banks or financial institutions for the specific or any other purpose, has not registered any charge or satisfaction of charge with the ROC, has not issued securities for a specific purpose, and holds no assets classified as held for sale. Authorised and paid-up equity share capital remained unchanged during the year, and no Foreign Direct Investment or External Commercial Borrowing was availed. The expansion-flavoured language in the MD&A - offshore delivery centres, acquisitions plugging AI and cloud capability gaps, hybrid delivery models - describes the global consulting industry, not this Company, and is not recorded as its own expansion.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects consultancy opportunities to increase in management consultancy, Artificial Intelligence, Digital Marketing and Blockchain, financial consultancy, information technology and market research
- Clients are becoming more professional and demanding and are seeking tangible results, shifting the consultant-client relationship toward a stronger, more intimate and mutually beneficial engagement
- Industry pivot from episodic advice and billable hours toward outcome-based / gain-share fee structures tied to measurable client metrics
- Generative AI and technology advisory demand from cloud migration, cybersecurity and AI-governance needs is a growth driver for the industry
- SMEs are the fastest-growing client base via fractional and subscription-based advisory models, while large enterprises still dominate spend
- Regulatory and ESG mandates, especially value-chain (Scope 3) decarbonisation, are creating long-term advisory pipelines
- Structural headwinds management flags for the industry: talent attrition to VC and product roles, IT-vendor bundling of strategy with implementation, and clients building in-house transformation teams

The Directors' Report states the Company is not engaged in manufacturing activity, so conservation-of-energy and technology-absorption particulars are not applicable, and refers only to 'editing facilities, offices etc.' where energy-conservation measures are taken. Schedule III additional regulatory information records that the Company has not borrowed any funds from banks or financial institutions for the specific or any other purpose, has not registered any charge or satisfaction of charge with the ROC, has not issued securities for a specific purpose, and holds no assets classified as held for sale. Authorised and paid-up equity share capital remained unchanged during the year, and no Foreign Direct Investment or External Commercial Borrowing was availed. The expansion-flavoured language in the MD&A - offshore delivery centres, acquisitions plugging AI and cloud capability gaps, hybrid delivery models - describes the global consulting industry, not this Company, and is not recorded as its own expansion.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Repeat-order orientation built on service quality and a stated service guarantee, per the MD&A Outlook
- Asset-light service model with no manufacturing activity, so conservation-of-energy and technology-absorption disclosures are not applicable
- Breadth of advisory offerings spanning strategy, project, financial, AI/technology and transaction (M&A, syndication) work under one roof
- No borrowings from banks or financial institutions for any purpose, and no charge registered with the ROC (Schedule III additional regulatory information)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Talent attrition and wage inflation — MD&A: firms face ongoing talent attrition as mid-career professionals leave for equity incentives in venture capital or product management roles; demand for practitioners versed in AI governance, advanced analytics and ESG outstrips supply, inflating compensation and compressing project margins. For an asset-light advisory firm whose only productive asset is its consultants, this is the core structural risk.
- Bundling by large IT delivery players — MD&A: massive IT delivery players such as TCS and Infosys frequently package strategy with implementation, undercutting pure-play advisory firms by up to 30%, directly pressuring the pricing of a small pure-play consultancy.
- Clients building in-house strategy and transformation teams — MD&A: corporate clients are rapidly expanding their own internal strategy and transformation departments, and internal centres of excellence absorb routine advisory functions, directly reducing reliance on external agencies.
- Freelance and platform disintermediation — MD&A: independent contractors and freelance platforms offer highly specialised, on-demand expertise at a fraction of the cost, challenging legacy consulting models and forcing a rethink of pricing strategies.
- Shift to outcome-based pricing and the burden of proving ROI — MD&A: clients are moving away from hourly billing toward gain-share and outcome-based fee structures tied to measurable metrics, and are strictly results-oriented; justifying premium fees without demonstrable metrics or milestone-based contracts is increasingly difficult, which transfers delivery risk onto the consultant.
- Industry skill gap and pace of technology change, particularly around AI — MD&A: a significant skill gap exists in the industry which could lead to a loss of revenue, since service quality depends entirely on the expertise and knowledge base of the people employed; capabilities are simultaneously transitioning toward deep tech integration, requiring continuous upskilling of the legacy workforce.
- Geographic and single-market concentration in India — The Company operates mainly in the Indian market and the Directors' Report states it neither earned nor used any foreign exchange during the period under review, so results are undiversified against a downturn in domestic consulting demand. Recorded as a structural concentration risk although the report does not label it as a risk.
- Tax and regulatory compliance exposure — The Directors' Report discloses a GST Show Cause Notice (No. 04/CGST/R-V/RBD/2025-26) received from the Kolkata South CGST & CX Commissionerate in respect of the Company's GSTIN, to which the Company submitted a reply; regulatory change is separately named in the MD&A as an external risk category.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Win repeat orders by delivering quality service backed by a service guarantee, with the value system centred on client satisfaction and adherence to work schedules (MD&A Outlook)
- Move up from advice into implementation - management states the consultant will increasingly be called upon to get involved in the implementation of recommendations
- Enhance consulting skills by staying current on trends and building analytical, problem-solving and client-communication capability, in response to a highly competitive Indian consulting industry
- Partner with other firms through joint ventures, alliances …

hero.oneLiner: Likhami Consulting Limited is an asset-light, India-focused advisory firm providing management, project, financial and technology consultancy services, in its 44th year of operation.
